task: ¿Tomarías un tren nocturno en lugar de un avión? Escribe 120–150 palabras comparando ambas opciones.
paragraphs: Not long ago, the sleeper train seemed destined to become a museum piece. Across Europe, operators were cancelling overnight routes that had run for decades, unable to compete with low-cost airlines offering tickets for the price of a sandwich. Why spend twelve hours rattling through the dark when you could fly in two?

Yet in the last decade, the night train has made a surprising comeback. In 2016, when Germany's national railway withdrew from the business, the Austrian operator ÖBB took over several of its routes under the brand Nightjet. Many observers thought the decision was risky. Instead, the trains proved so popular that new routes have since been added, linking cities such as Vienna, Berlin, Paris, Brussels and Amsterdam. Other operators, both public and private, have followed.

The most obvious reason for this revival is climate awareness. Depending on how the electricity is generated, a train journey can produce a small fraction of the carbon emissions of the equivalent flight. For travellers who want to reduce their footprint without giving up international travel, the sleeper offers an attractive compromise. The Swedish even have a word, "flygskam" or "flight shame", for the guilt some people feel about flying.

But the appeal is not only environmental. Many passengers simply enjoy the experience: going to sleep in one country and waking up in another, arriving in the city centre rather than at a distant airport, and avoiding long security queues. A night on the train also saves the cost of a hotel room.

Challenges remain. Sleeper carriages are expensive to build and maintain, and they earn money only once per day, unlike daytime trains, which can make several journeys. Ticket prices can therefore be high, and the most popular services sell out weeks in advance. Delays caused by engineering works or by differences between national rail systems can also frustrate travellers. Whether the night train becomes a mainstream option or remains a charming niche will depend largely on investment and political will.
